study.title: Jigsaw training-based background reverse attention transformer network for guidewire segmentation
study.venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery

imaging.modality_detail: Intraoperative X-ray fluoroscopy sequences during percutaneous coronary intervention

public_dataset_used.detail: Private dataset from three hospitals; authors state no public guidewire datasets exist

task.task_description: Single and dual guidewire segmentation in X-ray fluoroscopy sequences using an RPCA background map, a background reverse attention module on a TransUNet backbone, and a jigsaw training strategy that merges single-guidewire images into dual-guidewire images. Single guidewire set: 75 sequences (9266 frames, 23 cases); additional 19 dual-guidewire sequences (1247 frames) used only for testing.
task.clinical_application: Guidewire segmentation for percutaneous coronary intervention

architecture_names: Jigsaw training-based background reverse attention (BRA) transformer network

temporal_evidence.quote: the generated background map L and the current frame I are fed into the segmentation network to generate the guidewire segmentation result

method.class_imbalance_handling: Background reverse attention module to weaken background given foreground/background pixel imbalance; jigsaw strategy to compensate for scarce dual-guidewire data

comparators: Pyramid attention recurrent network (Zhou et al. 2020)

G1.quote: No public guidewire datasets are available for training and testing guidewire detection and segmentation networks.

G2.quote: there is a gap between the generated dual guidewire and the dual guidewire in the real world

G3.quote: segmentations for the entire X-ray fluoroscopy guidewire sequence were generated by passing the frames of the sequence one by one through our network

G5.quote: This step helps reduce the need for dual guidewire data and improve the performance of the network.
